shortName: Thomas F. Frist, Jr. College of Medicine at Belmont University
additionalCoursework: We recommend students seek out upper division hard science coursework that will help prepare them for the rigor of medical school. Courses like psychology, sociology, and statistics are also helpful. Applicants can major in any topic and be successful in our program.

medSchoolStudLife.diversity:
On of the values at the Frist College of Medicine is valuing difference. We believe our student body and community needs different voices and experiences to best serve our future patients. Our goal is to give space for diversity of thought through the lived narratives of our faculty, staff & students. Throughout the curriculum, the HEALER thread (Health Equity, Advocacy, Literacy, Education, and anti-Racism) provides programming to expand understanding of the social, cultural, economic, and political influences in patients’ perspectives and access to care, disparities in treatment and outcomes, and how physicians can deliver informed care as well as become advocates for health equity. Student organizations build on this curricular component including groups like AMSA, SNMA, LMSA, AMWA, CMDA/MCF. 

Students can seek out learning support through our Learning Support Team including free tutoring, academic coaching, learning style inventories, and individual learning plans for NBME exams.
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities:
Our goal is to foster student development as future physicians and leaders while creating a culture that embraces physical, mental/emotional, spiritual, financial, and social well-being. As a newer medical school, our students will have opportunities spanning student government and student life, national medical student associations, specialty interest groups, service groups, and wellness programs. https://www.belmont.edu/medicine/student-affairs/student-activities.html

Additionally, learning communities are essential for promoting student well-being and formation through strategic wellness initiatives and programs. Each student is placed in one of four 'Frist Houses' to gain academic support and professional development, while building community with their peers and faculty mentors in their medical school journey. Learn more: https://www.belmont.edu/medicine/student-affairs/wellness.html
medSchoolStudLife.setting:
Located just steps away from Music Row and two miles from the city center, living in Nashville provides quick access to all that the vibrant city has to offer. Along with being the Health Care Capital of the world, Nashville boasts small town charm, abundant green spaces, world-class music entertainment, live sports games and an unbeatable food scene. 

The medical school building opened in 2024 with the nearly 200,000-square-foot facility designed to create a fully interdisciplinary educational experience, allowing medical students to work alongside students in other health programs—just as they would in a clinical setting. The facility includes large lecture spaces designed for case-based learning, 50,000 square foot high-tech simulation center that utilizes virtual and augmented reality, dedicated library and study space, a parking garage, and ample dedicated study space. Learn more: https://www.belmont.edu/medicine/facilities.html & https://www.belmont.edu/engagement-simulation
medSchoolStudLife.housing: There are ample rental options near campus. A two-bedroom apartment in Nashville rents on average of $1900 per month ($950 per roommate). Accepted students will be given access to a list of housing options in the community curated by current students as well as connections to possible roommates. Learn more: https://www.belmont.edu/medicine/student-affairs/living-in-nashville.html
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems: Students have resources within the FCoM Student Affairs and Belonging office https://www.belmont.edu/medicine/student-affairs/ or Belmont University’s Office for Hope, Unity, and Belonging www.belmont.edu/hub
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystemsForDisabilities: Medical students have resources for support through the Learning Support team as well as Belmont's office of Accessibility Services: https://www.belmont.edu/accessibility/. Those seeking accommodations will be connected with Accessibility Services to navigate that process. On-going support is always available within FCoM's Learning Support Team. https://www.belmont.edu/medicine/student-affairs/student-success.html
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms:
Student wellness has been built into our foundation at the Frist College of Medicine. We know wellness is individual and personal so time has been allocated (at least three half days weekly) to be free for study, personal appointments, and wellness. At key transition points in the curriculum, Wellness Retreats are scheduled as part of the curriculum to focus on professional development, reflection, and selfcare. A Student Wellness Committee comes alongside members of the Student Affairs team to help address mental health issues, organize self-care events, and engage in mentoring, education, and health-related research. 

Our goal is to help students graduate medical school still in touch with the 'why' they matriculated medical school espousing. 

Learn more: https://www.belmont.edu/medicine/student-affairs/wellness.html
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture: At the Frist College of Medicine, we are looking for students who will help continue to build our collaborative culture. Healthcare is all about a team and with our small class sizes, this team mentality starts early. Throughout your foundational coursework, we have built in Impact Weeks following each foundation course designed to decompress, enhance interprofessional education opportunities with our Nursing, PT, OT, Pharmacy, Law, etc. students, and to give space to the bigger issues facing healthcare and healthcare providers today - Health Equity, Anti Racism, Leadership, etc. that will help our students be prepared for long healthy careers. Keeping wellness, collaboration, and community are at the core of our campus culture.
medSchoolStudLife.transportationAdditionalInfo: Preceptorships during M1 and clerkships during M3 are located throughout Nashville. Having access to a vehicle is recommended.

medSchoolCurriculum.dressCode: Professional dress is expected in simulated patient and patient settings. Casual dress is acceptable for non-clinical activities.
medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: A wide range of access points- professional learning specialists, tutoring, individual learning plans, & faculty with open door policies. www.belmont.edu/medicine/student-affairs/student-success.html
medSchoolCurriculum.patientInteraction: M1 and M2s work with standardized and simulated patients, and observe health professionals in clinical settings. This training prepares them to become active participants of the healthcare team.
medSchoolCurriculum.instructionStyle: Instructional style is focused on case-based active learning integrating basic and clinical sciences from day one. Students will utilize the simulation center focusing on hands on practice.
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations: Third year clerkships are completed in pediatrics, obstetrics and gynecology, internal medicine, family medicine, surgery, and psychiatry/neurology to be completed in the TriStar system in Nashville.
medSchoolCurriculum.lectureAttendance: Attendance is encouraged at all learning activities. Mandatory for Cases, PBL, Simulation, etc. while other activities are discretionary.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights:
At the Thomas F. Frist, Jr. College of Medicine, the curriculum is designed to prepare students to learn clinical reasoning and science, diagnose and treat patients through case-based learning, early and meaningful clinical experiences, and opportunities for experiences in medical research, ethics, health system science, interprofessional teams, and service learning. This early focus on the patient ensures FCoM students are prepared to excel in their residency program of their choice and become leaders who will help determine the solutions to tomorrow's healthcare challenges.

FCoM is committed to educating excellent future clinicians whose knowledge and clinical decision-making are firmly grounded in basic sciences and who consider the whole patient, with a deep and nuanced understanding of the socioeconomic and systems factors affecting health care. The M.D. curriculum features three distinct phases: the foundation phase (years 1 and 2), the clerkship phase (year 3), and the individualization phase (year 4).

Our educational philosophy focuses on bringing the basic sciences and clinical medicine together. Most courses are team taught with core clinician educator and scientist educator faculty teaching side-by-side in large and small-group settings. Emphasis is placed on active and self-directed learning, as well as frequent utilization of simulation. The centerpiece of the curriculum is clinical relevance. Weekly clinical cases will feature basic and clinical science principles in the context of social determinants of health as well as how gender, cultural, and other forms of diversity impact health outcomes. With an ultimate goal of training physicians who acknowledge and actively address how biases affect patient care, the curriculum will build from orientation through graduation to develop culturally competent physicians who are aware of bias in themselves and within their communities.
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms: FCoM students will be encouraged to explore their interests including primary care. During M1 and M2, all students will have a longitudinal experience with a preceptor where they will spend time in a primary care setting. Students build on this experience throughout the M3 clerkships and into M4 electives.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms: Optional electives between M1 and M2 are available as an opportunity to begin a project. FCoM is building on the foundation of Belmont University, HCA, and the extensive network in Nashville to provide students with opportunities in community-based research, bench research, and clinical research.
medSchoolCurriculum.academicSystemText: Learn more about our curriculum at https://www.belmont.edu/medicine/medical-education/.
medSchoolCurriculum.communityServiceText: Service learning is a tenet of Belmont University. FCoM students will have service learning embedded in the curriculum longitudinally as well as ample extracurricular opportunities.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchThesisText: Students may pursue research during electives between M1 and M2 years as well as throughout their fourth year.
medSchoolCurriculum.affiliatedHospitals: Tristar Medical Group Locations - Nashville, TN. Learn more: https://www.belmont.edu/medicine/medical-education/curriculum.html.
medSchoolCurriculum.gradingSystem: Grading during the foundational phase will be letter grade. Tiered grading for clerkship phase (Honors/High Pass/Pass/No Credit).

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation:
Belmont University is the perfect home for Nashville’s innovative, new medical school. Long known for its excellent education, dedicated faculty and student support, the Frist College of Medicine will provide opportunities with the institution’s longstanding partners across the health care community.

Our belief in a whole-person approach to health care informs everything we do – from curriculum design, to clinical experiences, and the faculty and staff supporting student learning. We are committed to educating excellent future clinicians whose knowledge and clinical decision-making are grounded in basic sciences and who consider the whole patient, with a deep and nuanced understanding of the socioeconomic and systems that affect health care.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement:
Our Mission: The Thomas F. Frist, Jr. College of Medicine at Belmont University is dedicated to cultivating diverse physician leaders of character who embrace a whole-person approach to healing in a community of service-learning, inspired by character and the love and grace of Christ.

Our Vision: Shaping medicine through transformative whole person care.

We are united by a common set of value statements:
Love Learning
Lead by Serving
Live with Integrity
Heal Together in Humility
Welcome Difference

Learn more: https://www.belmont.edu/medicine/about/

As a newer medical school, we are looking for students who see themselves in this mission and share these values. Our belief in a whole-person approach to health care informs everything we do – from education, to clinical experiences, to the leadership team we’ve selected. The focus is on you - from challenging academics and robust clinical experiences - it’s personalized education, informed at every level throughout medical school.

From the very beginning of the admissions process, FCoM considers each aspect of who you are and what you bring to the learning environment.  This focus on you continues when you become a student - with small class sizes, small group learning, and hands on practical experience, our community will support you as you grow into the type of physician you want to be.

medSchoolApplication.cbcRequired: Yes - a background check will be required by all accepted students prior to matriculation.
medSchoolApplication.applicantResponseToOffer: FCoM follows all AAMC recommendations and traffic rules.
medSchoolApplication.amcasLettersText:
If more than the required three letters of evaluation are received, they will remain in the file throughout the review process with the admissions committee focusing on the primary three letters. 

Letters of evaluation must come directly through the letter service and are not accepted directly.
medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance:
We are looking for three letters of evaluation from letter writers who are familiar with your work ethic, passion, drive, and service. While we know your selection of letter writers may vary, we would ideally ask for:
- one letter from a health care professional who has observed you in a clinical setting
- one letter from a faculty member who has taught you in a hard science course 
- one letter from an additional faculty member or a supervisor in a service setting 

Letter packets and committee letters are also accepted. All letters must be sent through the AMCAS letter service.
medSchoolApplication.typicalInterviewDay:
Candidates will be sent information to review and familiarize themselves with prior to the interview day. During the interview session, there will be plenty of time to ask questions and learn more about the topics important to you in selecting a medical school. 

Two interviews are conducted. One is a traditional open-file interview with a faculty member or member of the admissions committee lasting approximately 30 minutes. The second is a structured interview conducted by a member of the FCoM community that includes standard questions and the interviewer is blind to all application materials. This interview may feel similar to an MMI experience. 

As a newer school, the interview day is designed specifically to allow time for applicants to ask questions and learn more about areas of interest.
medSchoolApplication.interviewInvitations: We anticipate our first interview invitations being sent in August.
medSchoolApplication.interviewFormat: Two interviews are included – a traditional open file interview and a structured closed file interview. Each interview lasts 30 minutes. The rest of the interview session is designed for applicants to learn about FCoM and ask questions.
medSchoolApplication.regionalInterview: Regional interviews are not available. All interviews will be conducted virtually via Zoom. Accepted students will be invited to campus to visit.
medSchoolApplication.videoInterview: FCoM will conduct virtual interviews for the 2027 admissions cycle. Applicants can expect information and instructions via email.
medSchoolApplication.secApplSentTo: Selected applicants are invited to fill out the supplemental application, typically, we look for a 3.0 GPA and 500 MCAT score for supplemental application invitation.
medSchoolApplication.secApplEarliestDtText: Applicants are encouraged to complete the supplemental application within 2 weeks of receipt.

medSchoolApplication.additionalInfo:
FCoM reviews applications prior to extending supplemental application invitations. We typically are looking for our academic minimums which are a 3.0 GPA and 500 MCAT. Once the supplemental application is received, complete files are reviewed for interview invitation. During this review, all AMCAS and supplemental application materials are reviewed holistically looking for concordance with FCoM Mission, Vision, and Values. Our admissions committee will extend interview invitations on a rolling basis. Most interviews will be held on Friday afternoons. Candidates can expect email communication at each point in the admissions process to stay informed. We understand the time and dedication put into preparing for this application cycle and we are committed to clear communication. 

Following the interview, candidates are either offered admission, added to the waitlist, or released from the admissions process. Those offered admission are invited to a Second Look event in April. Admission offers are contingent on successful criminal background check, compliance with technical standards, documentation of a bachelor’s degree, and other pre-matriculation requirements. Accepted students will be given access to a website to track their progress on these requirements in May. 

Any questions about the process should be directed to FCoM Admissions at Medicine@belmont.edu.
medSchoolApplication.mcatScoresAdditionalInfo: FCoM will see all MCAT scores and will utilize the most recent total score.
medSchoolApplication.mcatScreenAdditionalInfo: In addition to other factors, we look for a 500 MCAT for supplemental application invitation.
medSchoolApplication.gpaScreenAdditionalInfo: In addition to other factors, we look for a 3.0 GPA for supplemental application invitation. A hybrid GPA of the most recent 60 hours will be utilized when post bacc or graduate coursework is available.
medSchoolApplication.minCreditHourInfo: We will weigh most heavily on the most recent 60 hours when graduate or postbacc work is present.
medSchoolApplication.courseworkAcceptanceInfo: We understand applicants have may different pathways to medical school. We encourage seeking out challenging and rigorous coursework and enrollment to be best prepared for the rigors of medical school.
medSchoolApplication.letterOfIntentAdditionalInfo: We utilize the information provided to us via the AMCAS application. If additional information is needed, candidates will be contacted directly. If significant updates or achievements have occurred, an email with a PDF can be sent to Medicine@belmont.edu or uploaded into our system.
medSchoolApplication.technicalStandardInfo:
Medical education requires the accumulation of scientific knowledge be accompanied by the simultaneous acquisition of skills and professional attitudes and behaviors. Qualified applicants must demonstrate the cognitive and physical abilities, and behavioral and communication skills required to complete a rigorous curriculum and meet certain technical standards for medical students and physicians. A graduate of the Frist College of Medicine at Belmont University must have the knowledge and skills to function in various clinical settings and to provide a wide spectrum of care. 

Applicants are provided with this document during the interview process, required to attest to it during the pre-matriculation process, and will have access to Belmont's Disability Services Office to navigate the accommodations process.

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid: The Belmont University Financial Aid Office  provided aid awards for students including scholarships and loans. Students receive counseling on financial aid issues and assistance in developing budgets for managing living and education expenses. Those receiving financial aid will receive in-depth, one- on-one counseling as well as information on monthly budgeting, loan disbursements, alternative loan programs, repayment options, and loan consolidation.

medSchoolAcceptance.waitlistInformation: The waitlist at FCoM is live and regularly reviewed. Those added to the waitlist could be invited to join the class at any time in the cycle.
medSchoolAcceptance.waitlistProcedure: The waitlist is live, unranked, and reviewed at each Admissions Committee meeting throughout the cycle. Candidates on the waitlist may be offered admission at any point in the cycle.

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec:
We encourage applicants to seek out courses that will not only prepare them for the MCAT, but to prepare them for the rigors of medical school - specifically upper division hard science coursework. We also recognize and appreciate that each applicant's path to medical school is unique and these unique paths will converge in a diverse group of learners. 

Coursework taken at a community college or for a pass/fail grade will be accepted.
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors:
Our holistic review process balances an applicant’s life experiences and qualities with their academic accomplishments. We are looking forward to getting to know you – your background, your passions, and your future goals - as you begin your life-long study of medicine.

From the very beginning of our process, FCoM considers each aspect of who you are and what you bring to the learning environment. We utilize a holistic review process valuing each applicant’s experiences, attributes, and academic metrics and how that aligns with the mission of the Frist College of Medicine.

Applicants are encouraged to reach out to Medicine@belmont.edu with any questions about the process.
medSchoolSelection.preMedShadowText: We encourage depth and breadth of clinical exposure. This exposure can be gained through shadowing, volunteering, or working in the healthcare field. We want our students to understand not only the role of the physician, but the importance of the healthcare team.
